notice: RN bank batch 128: Mental health case studies: depression with suicide risk, lithium toxicity, NMS and clozapine. Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026. See REVIEW-LOG.md.

questions.stem: Highlight the findings that raise this client's immediate suicide risk.

rationale.correct: A plan, means, prior attempt, alcohol and sudden calm early in treatment signal high risk.

perOption.r1: A specific plan with access to lethal means.
perOption.r3: Energy returns before mood lifts; a decision may have been made.
perOption.r6: Antidepressants carry a boxed warning for suicidality under 25.

references: Psychiatric-mental health nursing texts (e.g. Varcarolis; Halter)

questions.educationalObjective: Recognize cues of high suicide risk.

questions.stem: For each statement, indicate whether it is accurate or inaccurate about suicide risk.

rows.text: Asking directly about suicide does not plant the idea
Risk can rise in the first weeks of antidepressant treatment
A sudden improvement in mood can mean a decision to die
A no-suicide contract makes the client safe
Clients who talk about suicide rarely act on it

rationale.correct: Direct questions are safe; contracts are not protective.

perOption.r1:c1: Direct questions are safe and expected.
perOption.r1:c2: Direct questions are safe and expected.

questions.stem: On day 2, the client says, "Everyone would be better off without me." Which responses by the nurse are therapeutic? Select all that apply.

options.text: "Are you thinking about killing yourself right now?"
"You feel like a burden to the people around you."
"I'm going to stay with you. Tell me more about that."
"Don't say that. Your family loves you very much."
"Why would you think something like that about yourself?"

rationale.correct: Ask directly, reflect and stay present.

perOption.e: "Why" questions put the client on the defensive.

questions.stem: On day 9, the team considers discharge. For each finding, indicate whether it supports discharge or needs follow-up first.

questions.stem: At discharge, for each statement, indicate whether it shows understanding or needs more teaching.

rows.text: "I'll drink 2 to 3 liters of water a day and more in hot weather."
"I'll keep my salt intake about the same each day."
"If I get vomiting or diarrhea, I'll call my provider."
"Ibuprofen is fine for my back pain."
"I'll get my thyroid and kidney blood tests as scheduled."
"I'll start a low-salt diet to lose weight."

rationale.correct: Steady fluids and salt, avoid NSAIDs and keep lab tests.

questions.stem: Which parts of the long-term clozapine plan should the nurse include? Select all that apply.

options.text: Regular ANC monitoring per the schedule
A bowel regimen with a stimulant laxative
Weight, glucose and lipids
Tell the prescriber before stopping smoking
Use bulk-forming fiber alone for constipation
Stop clozapine for 2 weeks if a dose is missed and restart at the old dose

rationale.correct: ANC checks, a bowel plan, metabolic checks and alerting the prescriber about smoking changes.

perOption.d: Smoking lowers clozapine levels; quitting can cause toxicity.
perOption.e: Can worsen obstruction with slow transit.
perOption.f: Must be re-titrated after missed days.

caseStudies.title: Major depression with suicide risk early in SSRI treatment

exhibits.title: Admission to the mental health unit
exhibits.body: A 19-year-old college student with major depressive disorder started sertraline 12 days ago. Today the student's roommate brought the student in after finding a goodbye note. The student says, "I have more energy now, and I finally know what I need to do." The student has given away a guitar and a laptop this week.

rows.label: Plan
cells: Will take a bottle of the roommate's pills

rows.label: Columbia scale
cells: Positive for intent and preparatory behavior

rows.label: Alcohol
cells: Drinking alone most nights for 2 weeks

exhibits.title: Mental health unit, day 6
exhibits.body: A 42-year-old client admitted with acute mania takes lithium 900 mg twice daily. The client had a stomach virus with vomiting and diarrhea for 2 days and started ibuprofen for a sore back. Today the client is unsteady and has slurred speech.

exhibits.title: Mental health unit
exhibits.body: A 34-year-old client with schizophrenia was admitted 4 days ago with agitation and received haloperidol IM several times plus oral haloperidol. Today the client is stiff, sweaty and not answering questions.

exhibits.title: Clozapine clinic
exhibits.body: A 29-year-old client with treatment-resistant schizophrenia started clozapine 10 weeks ago. Voices have quieted for the first time in years. Today the client reports a sore throat and has not had a bowel movement in 5 days. The client smokes 20 cigarettes a day and plans to quit.
